_comment: QQQ SWING sleeve — 'base + z-ladder' (always net long). Holds a permanent BASE long (base_pct of the swing budget, a protected floor NEVER sold). The other (1-base_pct) is deployed in n_steps as QQQ dips below its rolling 10-day mean: add_ladder maps the vol-normalised deviation z (ln(price/10d-mean)/rolling_std) to a TARGET number of deployed steps — deeper dip => more steps => more capital, so a SHALLOW dip nibbles one step and a DEEP dip deploys the whole sleeve (magnitude-scaled, buys all dips). Shallow rungs added (-0.5σ) so even small dips buy a little. trim_ladder sells the trade sleeve back toward the base on a strong RIP (+2.5σ) to re-arm. Backtest (QQQ 2.5y, $24): +60% vs +49-53% for a raw %-drawdown ladder, which churned 25-52x — the rolling-mean z is smoother and captures multi-week dips without round-tripping. cooldown_days gates add/trim (not the base). long_only. Live sizing uses allocation.py swing_budget; 'capital' is a backtest fallback. Steps are RECONCILED from real QQQ shares each run (cloud_decide.decide_swing) so a drifted/optimistic ledger can't wedge the ladder at 'full' (the bug that made it sit out a selloff).
